A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MHL research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite internal inconsistencies in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments, masking and curriculum ablations, sensitivity studies, and a truncation experiment in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original recommendation experiments and reports additional reconstruction-weight, item-frequency, sequence-length, and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: The joint objectives, masking granularities, and three-phase curriculum remain. However, v2 Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1 specify exponential mask-ratio decay, while both v1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix I specify linear decay. This conflict prevents establishing whether the implemented scheduler changed. Expanded architecture details alone do not establish another method change.

E1.justification: The targeted truncation evaluation moves from Sports and Outdoors in v1 Appendix A to Toys and Games in v2 Appendix E. The main three Amazon categories and semantic-ID/raw-title next-item tasks remain; the additional frequency and length analyses subdivide existing test data.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same seven item-ID and five semantic-ID comparators. RPG remains the comparator for text-token generalization, the case study, and truncation. Newly added analyses also compare against RPG rather than introduce another baseline.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the codebook setting from 32 to 16. v2 reports dataset-specific settings, extends the codebook sweep from 8–64 to 4–64 and masking ratios from 0.10–0.25 to 0.05–0.40, and adds reconstruction-weight sweeps, subgroup evaluation, and a controlled single-GPU efficiency protocol. The main leave-one-out split and ranking metrics remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds reconstruction-loss-weight sensitivity, cold-item frequency analysis, sequence-length stratification, and computational-efficiency analysis, while extending existing hyperparameter studies. These address several previously untested questions. Curriculum ablations, title-token generalization, truncation, and the helmet case study already existed in v1.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.2 newly states that results average three runs with different random seeds; v1 provides no corresponding run-count statement. This establishes additional reporting, not necessarily increased replication. Neither version reports confidence intervals or standard deviations.

E6.justification: Many RPG, MHL, ablation, and sensitivity scores are replaced. For example, Table 1 Beauty NDCG@10 changes from 0.0460 to 0.0495 for MHL and from 0.0394 to 0.0436 for RPG. Revised Table 2 shows entropy-only masking below random masking throughout. New subgroup and efficiency results substantially expand the evidence; changed settings prevent treating these revisions as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal definitions of disjoint codebook-token ranges and position-specific mask-token allocation in Appendix A, plus normalized cosine-classifier probabilities in Appendix B. These extend the mathematical specification beyond v1. The cross-entropy and entropy framework remains, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The principal MHL, entropy-guidance, curriculum, and state-of-the-art contribution claims remain. v2's introduction newly asserts that existing models suffer performance collapse under truncation while MHL remains robust and exceeds the leading baseline by over 40%, strengthening the motivating empirical claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of cold-item performance, popularity effects, reconstruction-weight tradeoffs, and training overhead, together with explicit text-only and computational limitations. It also corrects the case-study interpretation from firearm-related interests to sports and protective equipment. These substantially expand the discussion of mechanisms and applicability.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with a stated available repository link and adds vocabulary allocation, prediction-head equations, training pseudocode, explicit text-token settings, and detailed runtime and memory information. Appendix E also clarifies that truncation changes the prediction target. These materially expand reproducibility information, although conflicting scheduler descriptions remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lin et al. (2025), Liu et al. (2025), and Rao et al. (2024, 2026), connecting the work to additional generative recommendation, salience-aware generation, and adaptive data-selection research. The central positioning against BERT4Rec, S3-Rec, and autoregressive recommenders remains.

P1.justification: The method section is substantially rewritten and reorganized around architecture, objectives, and online entropy computation. Appendices expand from A–C to A–J with redistributed explanations, and new Limitations, Ethics Statement, and Acknowledgements sections alter the document structure. Author and header information also changes.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, adds Figures 3–7, introduces notation and analysis tables, and relocates detailed sensitivity tables to the appendices. Existing text-token and case-study tables are reformatted, with relative-improvement columns added to the former. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful diagnostic analyses, three-seed reporting, implementation detail, and training-cost evidence. However, its new truncation-collapse claim conflicts with Table 10's higher truncated scores; revised Table 2 reverses the entropy-versus-random trend without correcting the superiority claim; and the new exponential scheduler conflicts with retained linear-decay instructions. These problems affect central conclusions and reproducibility. The substantial additions and substantive consistency problems do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
